paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. When God hands you a message, you carry it. Ezekiel is told, "I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel. Whenever you hear a word from My mouth, give them a warning from Me." (Ezekiel 3:17) A watchman who naps through the job is not a watchman, he's a very quiet person standing on a wall.

Now look at what God puts on the watchman. Ezekiel's job is to speak, not to make people listen. If he warns and the man won't turn, God says "you will have saved yourself." (Ezekiel 3:19) But if he stays silent, God says, "I will hold you responsible for his blood." (Ezekiel 3:18) So faithfulness is the whole assignment, and the results belong to God and to the one who hears.

And that's why this matters to you, baker. Ezekiel was bound, silent and shut in, and he could still speak only when God opened his mouth. God's last word to him is, "Whoever listens, let him listen; and whoever refuses, let him refuse." (Ezekiel 3:27) Listen to God's word, say what He says, and trust Him with the rest. The story isn't over, because Ezekiel's watchman work is just getting started.
